newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB tumbles further on profit concerns.
newsitem.headline: NAB tumbles further on profit concerns.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) shares tumbled in early trading on Friday, as investors continued to sell after the bank warned on Thursday of leaner profits.
At 0025 GMT (10.25 a.m.), NAB shares were trading 24 cents below Thursday's close at A$17.87 after earlier hitting a low of A$17.75.
A banking analyst said the renewed sell-off looked like an over-reaction by the market to NAB managing director Don Argus' warning that the bank's run of record profits could end.
"On our numbers, profit is going to pick up again in (the year to September 30) '98," the Melbourne-based analyst said.
"So what's happening is the margin contraction (on interest income) is washing through in the second half and things in Australia are going to be pretty tough."
In April, NAB implemented cuts on home lending rates of up to 70 basis points.
Argus said on Thursday, after unveiling a record half-year profit of A$1.14 billion for the six months ended March 31, said the margin squeeze would be felt in the current half year.
"Competition in all markets will be unrelenting and will place increasing pressure on the ability of the group to sustain its record profits," Argus said in a statement.
By 10.40 a.m. (0040 GMT), NAB shares were 26 cents lower at A$17.85.
